evidence.note: Agent entered plan mode and wrote an upfront plan.md for the whole build, signaling deliberate decomposition before coding rather than feature-to-feature improvisation.

TaskCreate markers form coarse ordered milestones — 'create the project foundation' → 'implement core FastAPI/Mastodon endpoints' → 'build remaining templates' — with implicit completion notes, broadly reflecting dependencies (foundation-first).

Foundational/gate-critical work front-loaded: mkdir skeleton, curl pinned vendored libs early (step 9), requirements.txt, start.sh, db.py/models.py/schemas.py before endpoints, health endpoint. Dependencies (storage/auth before API) are respected.

Middle becomes a reactive patch stream walking requirement categories (admin scoping, idempotency, cache validators, CSRF, cookie-name fix, seed admin/user split, SSE, profiles, threads, errors) — coverage-conscious breadth across the surface, but driven by gap-auditing rather than a maintained milestone hierarchy with explicit per-milestone exit checks or re-ordering.

reasoning: The agent produced a sensible ordered plan with coarse milestones (foundation → core API → UI) whose sequencing broadly reflects dependencies and front-loads gate-critical items (pinned libs, storage, auth, health), matching the level-5 anchor. It goes slightly beyond by deliberately allocating effort across the wide surface (admin, idempotency, cache, CSRF, SSE, seed, threads) rather than gold-plating one feature, but the milestones carry only implicit done-criteria — no explicit verifiable exit checks — and the mid-build is a reactive patch stream rather than an actively re-planned, coverage-tracked hierarchy, keeping it well below the level-8/10 anchors.
